newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn stands firm on return of Bosnian refugees.
newsitem.headline: Bonn stands firm on return of Bosnian refugees.

text.p: The German government on Wednesday stood by its plan to start sending home 320,000 Bosnian refugees next month despite heavy criticism from the United Nations refugee agency and humanitarian groups.
"We are of the opinion that the repatriation can begin on October 1," an interior ministry spokesman said, a day before the 16 federal states work out a schedule for sending the refugees back.
Guenter Beckstein, interior minister of the southern state of Bavaria, compared the refugees' situation to that of Germans rebuilding their ravaged country after World War Two.
"We know how hard rebuilding is. Looking at the situation in Bosnia, the possibilities are already much, much more favourable than they were for the Germans after World War Two," he said.

"Military security is completely established," he added. "Unfortunately the process of ethnic separation continues, but there are safe areas for everyone in Bosnia within their respective ethnic groups."

Germany harbours 320,000 Bosnian refugees, more than the rest of the European Union combined, and plans to start gradual forced repatriations in October if refugees refuse to go voluntarily. It will begin with single adults and childless couples.

But the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) says 60 percent of Bosnian refugees in Germany are Moslems from areas that were ethnically cleansed by Serbs and it would be dangerous for them to return home now.

The UNHCR representative in Germany, Judith Kumin, said it was too soon to send back refugees who did not want to go. No refugees should be sent back to homes in regions dominated by another ethnic group, she said.
Even in 22 regions which the UNHCR had singled out for the return of refugees, 31,000 homes needed to be repaired before 185,000 people could return, Kumin said in a statement.
Ekkehard Wienholtz, interior minister of Schleswig-Holstein, said his state would not make any of the 4,100 refugees living there leave against their will before April 1 at the earliest.

He said refugees should not be forced to leave while human rights abuse and massive resistance to returnees from different ethnic groups continued, and while there was still no effective administration to supervise their return.
